title: Choose the Projects page structure
question: The design system is settled; this choice is how /projects is arranged. All three keep the About skill links landing on a marked project. The roll dealt Status Bands first. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Status Bands
options.lineage: Home's label-and-body sections, one per station
options.thesis: The page divides into Ongoing, In progress, Shipped and Archive, each status a section holding its projects, in the station order Home uses.
options.viewport: Title over a station key that doubles as contents with counts; the Ongoing band opens with Homelab and Document pipeline in Home's row form.
options.risk: Two projects per band makes thin sections, and the stations on each row repeat what the band already says.

options.label: Quarter Board
options.lineage: The Home chart's four six-hour quarters, one per status
options.thesis: Four columns on the quarter lines hold Ongoing, In progress, Shipped and Archive, so the whole record sits on one sheet.
materials: archive names in the last quarter
options.viewport: Title, then four columns headed by station cells; each featured project sits in its status column, the archive names filling the fourth.
options.risk: Quarter columns hold about 40 characters a line, so long descriptions run tall, and the board can read like a kanban.

options.label: Project Datasheets
options.lineage: About's datasheet front page, one per project
options.thesis: Each featured project gets a sheet: its name in the wide cut, the description as the reading column, and a ruled table of status, tech and source beside it.
options.viewport: Title, then the Homelab sheet: name in the wide cut, description on the left half, Status, Built with and Source in a ruled table on the right.
options.risk: One paragraph per project leaves each sheet lighter than a datasheet promises, and six sheets make a long scroll before the archive.
